description: High school engineer and member of the Ralph Vellon Engineering Academy. Interested in software engineering, aerospace system design, and competitive STEM projects! Currently building my computer science toolkit through Harvard's CS50 and specializing in Python-driven simulations. I am working as a solo builder for Space Apps 2026 to push my development and creative skills to their limits and build a high-impact space educational tool that can help and inspire younger generations of students.
summary: SOL 15: Mars Outpost Commander is based on real, live NASA data to show players the real constraints and trade-offs. I also developed multiple conditions, such as Junior Cadet 7-9 mode and Mission Commander 10-12, so it can accommodate a wide range of players. The player commands a 4-person Mars habitat for 15 Sols (Martian days) by balancing a 100 kw power grid across MOXIE oxygen, hydroponics, water, radiation shielding, and science. The hands-on trade-offs that happen during the mission teach systems engineering better than a book. For example, I playtested with a younger student, and it proved that players can quickly figure out power trade-offs on their own! Additionally, for those who have a strong knowledge of Spanish, an English/Spanish bilingual toggle is included along with clickable inline Mars glossaries!
details:
1. DETAILED PROJECT DESCRIPTION

What SOL 15: Mars Outpost Commander Does |

SOL 15: Mars Outpost Commander is an interactive, zero-install Mars survival and systems engineering simulator designed for K-12 students (ages 7-12+). Players step into the role of a Habitat Commander for a 4-person NASA surface outpost across 15 Sols (Martian days, 24 hours 39 minutes each). Rather than relying on passive worksheets or unrealistic sci-fi tropes, the simulator requires students to balance a constrained 100 kW Kilopower + solar grid across four critical life support subsystems (MOXIE Oxygen Generation, Closed-Loop Hydroponics, Water-Wall Radiation & Thermal Shielding, and Science & Earth Comms), while surviving real Martian dust storms, solar particle events, radiation, and greenhouse contamination hazards.

  1. Live NASA DONKI Space Weather Connection: Queries NASA's CMEAnalysis API on launch to fetch real Coronal Mass Ejection shock speeds and Mars impact predictions, seamlessly falling back to a verified 726 km/s Mars CME archive record when offline.
  2. Instant Bilingual Localization (EN/ES): Switches the entire simulation, hazard alerts, glossary pop-up definitions, and printable certificate between English and Spanish with zero page reloads!
  3. Dual Tier Pedagogical Difficulty: Lets learners and players choose Junior Cadet (ages 7-9, gentler life support trade-offs and guided hints) or Mission Commander (ages 10-12+, full engineering constraints and resource trade-offs).
  4. NASA Mars Trek Landing Site Selection: Compares real Martian elevation and atmospheric physics between Ares Horizon Station in Jezero Crater (-2,570 m, +25% biosignature science bonus) and Olympus Deep Outpost in Hellas Planitia (-7,152 m, +20% MOXIE oxygen efficiency from higher air pressure, balanced against stronger dust storms).

How It Works - Key Technical & Scientific Innovations |

Real-Time Vital Forecasting & Resource Balance Model: Every 5 kW power adjustment updates next Sol vital predictions in real time using deterministic resource balance equations (Net Delta = Generation - Daily Crew Drain ± Active Hazard Modifier). Players see exact percentage deltas for Oxygen (+6.5% per 10 kW), Food & Water (+4.5% per 10 kW)< Radiation/Thermal Shielding (+4.0% per 10 kW), and Crew Morale (+2.0% per 10 kW) before advancing to the next Sol.

Difficulty Drain Calibration & Martian Physics:

  • Junior Cadet Calibration (Ages 7-9): Daily life-support drains are tuned to 14% O2, 11% Food, 9% Shielding, and 1% Morale per Sol so younger learners can experiment safely.
  • Mission Commander Calibration (Ages 10-12+): Daily drains increase to 18% O2, 15% Food, 12% Shielding, and 2% Morale per Sol, while dust fronts keep the total grid capacity at 75 kW (Jezero Crater) or 65 kW (Hellas Planitia).
  • Surface Radiation Dosimetry (NASA OSDR Radlab): Grounded in Curiosity RAD measurements (0.64 mSv/Sol), forcing players to maintain water wall shielding against cosmic rays and solar proton spikes.

IMAGE SHOWCASES:

- Active Mission Dashboard

- Habitat Exterior/Command Deck POV

- Power Sliders

- Live Vital Predictions

Gemini 2.5 Flash AI Advisor & 14-Minute Signal Delay: Integrated Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash API (requestGeminiHint in script.js) inside the Mission Control Advisor. When a student requests a hint, the app simulates the physical 14-minute Earth-to-Mars light-time radio delay before sending live habitat vitals, Sol count, difficulty tier, and power distribution to Gemini to generate a guided, age-appropriate engineering recommendation (with a deterministic local rule engine backup when offline).

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Interactive Space Science Glossary & POV Viewport: Includes clickable inline glossary popups (Sol, MOXIE, CME, Kilopower, Hydroponics, Perchlorates, Mars Trek) and an HTML5 Canvas viewport featuring a dynamic Martian Day/Night cycle with an instant Exterior Outpost/Command Deck Window POV switching!

Benefits, Classroom Validation & Sol-15 Debrief:

  • Classroom Playtesting & Accessibility | Playtesting with a younger student confirmed that real-time vital delta previews allow kids to grasp energy trade-offs intuitively without memorizing formulas. Built in zero-dependency HTML5 Canvas, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript with no login barriers, it runs smoothly on school Chromebooks and tablets!
  • Sol-15 Engineering Debrief, Starship Resupply & Certificate | Surviving all 15 Sols unlocks a full vital-history chart, an engineering log explaining every hazard decision, a realistic Sol-15 SpaceX Starship Cargo Resupply manifest (28,500 kg payload across purified water tanks, liquid oxygen, dust-resistant solar arrays, and hydroponic seed kits grounded in CSA Space Food Toolkit data), and a downloadable Certificate of Mars Exploration customized with the student's name, rank, landing site, and science score.

FAILED MISSION | *Notice how no certificate is available to download because you need to pass the mission.

PASSED MISSION | Self-explanatory - *Lets you download your certificate with accurate game credentials!

CERTIFICATE & SpaceX Resupply Debrief |

Tools, Coding Languages & Public Links:

  • Frontend & Graphics: HTML5 Canva, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+).
  • APIs & Open Data: NASA DONKI (CMEAnalysis), NASA Mars Trek, NASA OSFR RedLab, Canadian Space Agency (CSA) Space Food Toolkit, Google Gemini API (gemini-2.5-flash).
  • Deployment & Source Code: Hosted live on GitHub Pages (https://bermudez-carlos.github.io/mars-outpost-command/) with full open-source code on GitHub (https://github.com/Bermudez-Carlos/mars-outpost-command) and a 7-slide presentation deck (https://canva.link/p8ahxfcdkda9k21)
  • Acknowledgement of Super Intelligence (SI) Tools: Google Gemini, ChatGPT, and GitHub Copilot were used during development to assist with NASA DONKI JSON parsing, CSS/JavaScript UI debugging, click audio sounds, and bilingual English/Spanish educational phrasing. No SI tools were used to generate or alter any NASA logos or official branding.
  • Zero AI-Generated Media: All habitat canvas graphics, UI icons, and layouts were custom-coded in HTML5 Canvas and CSS3 with the aid of VS Code Copilot; no SI tools were used to generate images.
Benefits & Long-Term Educational Goals:
  • Immediate Classroom Value: Removes hardware and setup barriers, as any K-12 teacher or student can launch the trainer in one click on a school Chromebook or tablet in English or Spanish without creating an account
  • Systems Engineering Intuition - Instead of trying to memorize space facts, students get to learn how real planetary constraints such as elevation, air pressure, solar irradiance, and radiation dose force interconnected trade-offs across oxygen, food, shielding, and science.
  • Inspiring Future Explorers: Basing every mission parameter on authentic NASA and CSA telemetry shows young learners that spaceflight engineering is accessible, measurable, and solvable.

Strategic Roadmap for Future Expansion:

  • Phase 1 --> Live Mars Surface Weather (NASA Curiosity REMS): Connect daily atmospheric live pressure, ground/air temperature, and UV radiation telemetry from Gale Crater so habitat thermal and power drains respond to real Martian seasons.
  • Phase 2 --> Kid-Friendly Visual Resource Summary+Graph Visualization (Ages 7-9): Add an icon-based resource breakdown (grouped oxygen tanks, food crates, shield blocks, and morale icons) along the Sol-15 line graph directly inspired by NYC judge feedback to make post-mission analytics even easier for younger cadets to understand.
  • Phase 3 --> Classroom Teacher Dashboard & Co-Op Missions: Enable multi-student classroom work sessions where teams manage/control adjacent Mars modules (Life Support, Power Grid, Science Lab) and share a class code for a teacher to progress tracking.
